summary: Staggered prefetch wave causes ephemeral GPU scarcity and autoscaler credit drain in dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary: During two midday warm-up windows (11:45–12:10 & 12:40–13:00 PDT) the customer's dedicated pool experienced repeated short-lived GPU shortages that triggered fallback routing and a p50/p99 throughput degradation. Symptoms looked like noisy-neighbor prefetch rollovers where many tenant connections simultaneously requested KV/prefetch work and drove allocator credit depletion.

Impact: Customer reported ~25% effective throughput loss for latency-sensitive batched routes and ~30% increase in fallback to hosted variants. User-facing applications experienced spikes of 5xx errors for a small subset of requests and sustained increase in tail latency for 15–20 minutes during each window.

Environment: Dedicated pool (CanopyAI reserved cluster), prod-us-west, autoscaler configured with conservative cooldown (300s) and token-based credit accounting. Prefetch subsystem uses eager per-connection prefetch for long-lived streams.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Sudden arrival of many long-lived chat streams from customer-side release at T0.
2) Streams hit prefetch logic synchronously; multiple sidecars initiate KV warmup and large prefetch batches at near-identical times.
3) Allocator issues large short-lived slot reservations; GPU credit counters decrement rapidly and trigger short backoffs and attach failures.
4) Autoscaler sees transient exhaustion and delays provisioning due to cooldown, causing routing to fall back to cheaper hosted model variants.

Observed metrics & logs: CPU-side prefetch queue depth spike (x7 baseline), allocator_credit_balance dropped to 8% sustained for ~90s, attach latency peaked at 3.4s (baseline 120ms), per-GPU nvlink-util increased 2x, scheduler logs show repeated "slot-reserve-timeout" entries during each surge. No GPU driver kernel crashes observed. Sidecar logs reference repeated prefetch RPC retries (grpc DEADLINE_EXCEEDED) and connection churn.

Initial hypothesis: Synchronous prefetch waves (customer release cadence) combined with token-credit conservative policy and autoscaler cooldown caused transient GPU scarcity. Prefetch behavior is effectively a "thundering prefetch" that starves allocation and prevents the autoscaler from reacting quickly because of cooldown hysteresis.

Customer notes: CanopyAI reports they deployed a client-side change that re-establishes many long-lived streams at once (internal release orchestration), which matches surge timing. They confirmed no change to model pins.
investigation_notes: 03-13T12:05 PDT: Correlated increase in long-lived connections from customer IP block 34.122.9.0/24 with prefetch queue depth spike.
Heap/kv cache growth observed but not beyond OOM thresholds — issue not a memory leak.
Allocator debug dump: lots of tiny short-lived reservations and immediate releases; pattern matches synchronous warmup rather than steady load.
Autoscaler traces show cooldown prevented immediate scale-up; recent config uses 300s cooldown to avoid flapping.
No kernel or driver faults; GPU telemetry shows elevated nvlink and PCIe utilization implying IO-heavy prefetch traffic.
Hypothesis validated by reproducing with synthetic long-lived stream generator in staging that triggers synchronous prefetch waves and alloc-credit exhaustion.
Quick mitigation tested in staging: rate-limit prefetch requests per-connection and add jitter to warmup reduced peak attach latency by ~60% in test runs.
Consideration: global throttles affect all tenants; we prefer targeted per-tenant admission control for dedicated pools.
Follow-up: evaluate autoscaler cooldown reduction and per-tenant prefetch pacing as combined fix.
Related runbook: dedicated-prefetch-playbook updated with investigation snapshot and recommended mitigations.

resolution: Workaround: temporary per-tenant prefetch cap applied to CanopyAI and a limited cooldown reduction on a subset of autoscaler nodes. Fix in progress: (a) sidecar prefetch jitter/backoff PR merged to canary (see PR #4987), (b) scheduler change to support per-tenant admission control planned, (c) autoscaler tuning RFC created. Customer mitigated client behavior by staggering warmups. Follow-up actions: full rollout of prefetch pacing, evaluate autoscaler cooldown tradeoffs, update runbook and add alert for 'synchronous-prefetch-wave' event.
